/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 21 July 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2670 (-1)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3930 (41)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2181 (-46)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1730 (-8)
Baltic Handysize Index: 903 (2)
CAPESIZE
The market posted a modest recovery today, with sentiment showing tentative signs of improvement across both the Pacific and Atlantic basins despite trading activity remaining relatively subdued. The BCI 182 5TC index edged up by $369 to $35,640. The C5 index was largely unchanged, rising by 0.1245 to $11.125, while the C3 route gained 0.195 to finish at $32.30. In the Pacific, confidence improved modestly. Although only one major miner was active, the return of several C5 operators helped bolster demand, contributing to a stabilisation in sentiment following recent weakness. Trading remained relatively thin, with offers opening in the mid-to-high $11s against an early bid of $10.75. The sole miner concluded a couple of fixtures at $11.10, while operators were indicating they could pay in the $11.00-$11.25 range, suggesting a narrowing gap between bids and offers. Atlantic sentiment also firmed slightly. Underlying cargo demand remained healthy, with reports of C3 fixing at $32.15 encouraging owners to push index-date offers above $33. However, bids remained closer to $32, resulting in limited fixture activity.
PANAMAX
Negative sentiment was evident across both basins today, with the P5TC declining by $416 to close at $19,629. Market activity remains subdued with brokers reporting limited enquiry on trans Atlantic routes and suggesting that the few discussions taking place are generally below last done levels. Some market sources have highlighted that mineral fronthaul supply appears to be providing a slightly more encouraging picture, with some improvement in activity and vessel supply continuing to look relatively tight. In the Pacific a lack of fresh enquiry continues to weigh on sentiment. The North Pacific has been particularly quiet, with very few fresh cargoes entering the market. Both the North Pacific and Australia have seen vessel availability increase, adding further pressure on rates. The W-Smash (82,742 2013) open Chiba 20 July was reportedly fixed for a trip via East Coast Australia to China, although there was some debate surrounding the achieved rate. Similarly, the CL Dalian (81,578 2014) also open Chiba 21/23 July was said to have fixed a coal cargo from the North Pacific, with no further details currently available. The Horizon Diamond (76,048 2011) open in Hong Kong 26-30 July fixed around $14,500 for a run from Indonesia to South China while the Zhun Xing 9 (81,586 2012) open Dongguan 22 July fixed for an Indonesia round at $16,500, on both the Charterer unknown. The Sasebo Glory (85,020 2016) open Onahama 17 July fixed a Pacific round in the high $19,000's and the Minoan Ocean (93,146 2011) open Huangpu 20 July was said to have fixed for an Australia round, with no other details heard. On the period side activity has been more noticeable, with several fixtures reportedly concluded for durations of around one year, providing a rare bright spot in an otherwise subdued market.
SUPRAMAX
After collecting and assessing yesterday, things began to return to normal today. The 11TC average was down $102 to $21,863 with the North American routes again taking a hit, especially the fronthaul. The East Mediterranean remains the positive area in the Atlantic, however concluded trades are scarce. In Asia it was mixed with the North showing some negative sentiment, whilst currently South East Asia remains positive with several Ultramaxs reported at $18,000 basis delivery Singapore for trips China, with the Indian Ocean still active and rates relatively flat.

Atlantic

The Capricorn Honor (56,732 2009) fixed delivery Marmara end July for a trip via the Russian Black Sea to the Far East at close to $30,000 reports said and Aries Bulk was linked with the HG Brisbane (57,802 2010) delivery Puerto Limon 24 July for 2 laden legs redelivery Singapore-Japan at $24,000.

Asia

The Norse Endurance (63,700 2026) Busan 23 July went on subjects for a trip via NoPac redelivery China at $19,000 and the SSI Invincible II (56,815 2012) prompt in Kandla fixed to the Far East with intention salt in the high $13,000’s with Aequor. Oldendorff were said to have booked a Tata steels cargo and taken the Desert Honour (63,462 2020) from Haldia for the trip via EC India redelivery Brownsville intention steels at $13,000 to cover it, whilst the Sheng An Hai (56,564 2012) Mtwara end July went on subjects for a trip via Richards Bay redelivery Pakistan at $24,000, but the Charterer was not disclosed.
HANDYSIZE
Following on from yesterday the market saw another subdued session, with limited activity emerging. The BHSI edged up by 2 points to 903, while the 7TC average increased by $31 to settle at $16,255. In the Continent and Mediterranean conditions remained flat, with little visible movement. The US Gulf and South Atlantic extended their downward trend, as ongoing tonnage oversupply continued to weigh on rates and push levels lower. Meanwhile Asia saw a positive turn, with both Owners and Charterers reassessing their positions. Sources noted that more fresh cargoes and healthy backhaul orders could lift rate expectations.

Atlantic
The Grace C (36,903 2013) open EC Central America was reported fixed for an inter-Caribbean trip at $18,500 by Pacnav, although further details were not disclosed. In addition the Sirius (37,705 2011) open NC South America was updated that fixed via US East Coast to the East Mediterranean with scrap at $21,500 by Sims, although further details were not disclosed.

Asia
A 35,000-dwt was heard fixed for a trip delivery Yeosu via EC India to redelivery Singapore at $12,000, although further details were not confirmed.

Market Fundamentals
BHP Port Talks Resume, Easing Near-Term Supply Risk

BHP and unions representing around 450 workers at Port Hedland have resumed negotiations over a four-year enterprise agreement, with talks set to continue on July 28 after some progress was made, Reuters reports. The development eases immediate concerns over disruptions at the key Western Australian export hub, following an eight-hour strike involving more than 100 workers last week. According to vessel tracking data, BHP’s Nelson point facility at Port Hedland handles around 12 Mt of iron ore exports per month on average, making prolonged industrial action a potential threat to supply. ai_analysis.summary: 干散货市场21日呈现分化走势，Capesize小幅反弹（BCI+41至3930），Handysize微升（+2至903），但Panamax和Supramax继续承压（BPI-46至2181，BSI-8至1730）。大西洋和太平洋盆地供需结构差异明显，C3跨大西洋航线情绪改善，C5太平洋航线情绪企稳但成交稀薄。FFA曲线显示短期合约承压，Q3 26各船型均有回落，市场对近月预期谨慎。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: Capesize市场出现温和反弹，BCI 5TC升至$35,640，C3/C5航线均小幅上扬。大西洋市场情绪边际改善，巴西矿商活跃推升C3报价至$32.15上方。Panamax持续走弱，P5TC跌$416至$19,629，太平洋供应过剩压制费率。Supramax 11TC平均跌$102至$21,863，美洲航线受冲击最大。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: Capesize：C3大西洋挺价信号明确（$32.15已成交，报价超$33），FFA Q3'26合约$34,100仍高于现货$32,300。Panamax：供需失衡显著（太平洋10日船期90艘vs需求25单），短期情绪偏空。Supramax：亚洲东南部挺价（Ultramax新加坡交船$18,000），印度洋平稳。Handysize：亚洲转暖信号出现。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注C3大西洋航线突破$33的持续性，若矿商继续出货有望提振Capesize整体情绪。Panamax跨太平洋航线供应压力需观察后续货量变化。FFA市场Capesize Aug'26报价$32,300-32,500，与现货贴水较大，可关注期现收敛机会。

跨大西洋航线持续走弱，$21,468较上期跌逾$1,000，供应过剩压制费率，短期无明显支撑
